related_questions.question: What are the 5 standard practices of infection control?

text_blocks.snippet: The five standard precautions for infection control are: hand hygiene, personal protective equipment (PPE), respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette, safe injection practices (including sharps safety), and environmental cleaning and disinfection. These precautions are implemented for all patients in all healthcare settings to prevent the transmission of infectious agents.
snippet_highlighted_words: hand hygiene, personal protective equipment (PPE), respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette, safe injection practices (including sharps safety), and environmental cleaning and disinfection

list.title: 1. Hand hygiene:
list.snippet: This involves frequent and thorough handwashing with soap and water or using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer.

list.title: 2. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE):
list.snippet: This includes items like gloves, gowns, masks, and eye protection, used to prevent exposure to blood, body fluids, secretions, and excretions.

list.title: 3. Respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette:
list.snippet: This involves covering coughs and sneezes with a tissue or elbow, and disposing of used tissues promptly.

list.title: 4. Safe injection practices (including sharps safety):
list.snippet: This includes using sterile needles and syringes, disposing of sharps in designated containers, and avoiding recapping needles.

list.title: 5. Environmental cleaning and disinfection:
list.snippet: This involves regularly cleaning and disinfecting surfaces and equipment to minimize the risk of contamination.
